validated_work_order.approach:
Change the key at the render site; do not touch the three entity identities. This is what the ticket asks for, and reading the code says it is also the only safe place to change it: `id: ''` is load-bearing downstream in ways a distinct id would silently break.

The check I ran for each candidate lookup that matches on `id`:

- filterHiddenItems.ts:34-47 discriminates the three rows on `item.uncategorized_id`, not id — unaffected either way.
- recalculate.ts:64 and :81, and the same pair in custom-spreadsheet.ts:212-235, match a row with `asset[groupByLabel] === (item.id ?? null) || (item.uncategorized_id && groupsByCategory)`. With id `''` the first clause is false and the second carries the row; a distinct id would make the first clause false too, so amounts would not move — but see showActivity below.
- narrowCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts:126-166) builds its keep-set from the real category list and runs before categoryLists() appends the synthetic rows, so the synthetic block is never narrowed away.
- calculateLegend.ts:70-73 sets `dataKey: item.id || item.name` and custom-spreadsheet.ts:277 sets `stacked[item.id || item.name]` from the same expression, so giving the rows real ids would move both together — a wide, chart-visible change for no benefit here.
- showActivity.ts:57-79 is the one that decides it. For the Uncategorized row the drilldown passes `field: 'category', id: '', uncategorizedId: 'other'`; `id && { ... }` is falsy on the empty string, so no category condition is emitted and the filter list is unchanged. Give the row `id: 'uncategorized'` and the same click emits `category is 'uncategorized'`, a filter that matches no category and turns the row's drilldown into an empty result. That is a behaviour change, in the opposite direction from the ticket's goal.
- CategorySelector never sees these rows (ReportSidebar.tsx:701 passes raw `categories.grouped`), so changing ids would not have broken its checkbox matching either — but it would have put a lie in the code for the next reader.

So: one line. At ReportTableList.tsx:77 replace `key={category.id}` with a key derived from the field that actually distinguishes these rows. `recalculate` (recalculate.ts:127) already copies `uncategorized_id` onto every row as `uncategorizedId`, and the type carries it (GroupedEntity, packages/loot-core/src/types/models/reports.ts:114-128), so the render site has what it needs without touching ReportOptions.ts:

    key={category.uncategorizedId ?? category.id}

For the three synthetic rows this yields 'other', 'transfer', 'off_budget'; for every real category `uncategorizedId` is undefined and the key stays the uuid it is today, so no existing row's key changes. A real category id cannot equal 'other'/'transfer'/'off_budget' (ids are uuids), and the three members live in one group with no real members, so the keys are distinct within the sibling list.

Add a comment at that line saying why: the three synthetic rows share `id: ''` on purpose and `uncategorizedId` is the field that tells them apart.

What this deliberately does not touch: the row values, the amounts, the group, the sidebar, the legend, and the graph dataKeys. Nothing a person sees on the screen changes, which is AC-2.

Reconciliation note for the reviewer: changing the key changes which DOM node React reuses for these three rows. ReportTableRow holds no per-row state (it is presentational plus click handlers), so there is nothing to leak between rows, and the change is in the direction of React doing the right thing — under duplicate keys it was already reusing the wrong nodes.

Two surfaces, and both are planned here:

1. Code plus a unit test that renders ReportTableList with a fixture holding the three synthetic rows and asserts no duplicate-key console.error, plus the e2e guard on the real screen. Unit test in packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/graphs/tableGraph/ReportTableList.test.tsx, new. It renders ReportTableList directly and passes a trivial `renderRow`, so ReportTableRow — and with it useNavigate, useFormat and useCategories — never mounts. Precedent for a jsdom render that pulls in `#components/table`'s Row: SidebarGroup.test.tsx and TransactionsTable.test.tsx.
2. An e2e case in the existing `custom reports` describe in packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts, watching the console channel for /same key/i while driving the exact repro (Mode=Total, Data Table, Show empty rows). The file already has the page-error settle constant and the neighbouring 'Rows follow the category selection when "show empty rows" is on' test walks this same path today without asserting the console. schedules.test.ts has the console-listener shape to copy.

No user-facing copy, layout, keyboard, focus or contrast surface changes: the fix alters a React key and nothing a person can see or operate. The empty/error/loading states of this screen are unchanged, because the screen is unchanged.
assumptions: The default custom report has Group by=Category (ReportOptions.ts:21, defaultReport), which is what routes ReportTableList into the grouped branch where the duplicate keys occur. If a user's report is grouped by Group, CategoryGroup, Payee, Account or Interval, the flat branch keys by index at ReportTableList.tsx:55 and the warning does not appear — consistent with the ticket naming the default configuration.

React 19.2.7 (packages/desktop-client/package.json:194) is what emits 'Encountered two children with the same key', and it does so via console.error in development builds. The jsdom unit test and the e2e case both rely on that.
Real category ids are uuids, so no real id can equal 'other', 'transfer' or 'off_budget'. That is what makes `uncategorizedId ?? id` collision-free without a prefix.

files.change: At line 77, inside the `item.categories.map(...)` that renders each group's member rows, change `key={category.id}` to `key={category.uncategorizedId ?? category.id}`. Leave the `index={i}` prop, the `parent_index={index}` prop, the surrounding `<View>` elements and the `key={index}` on the group row at line 55 exactly as they are. Add a short comment above the `key` explaining that Uncategorized, Transfers and Off budget all carry `id: ''` deliberately — the empty id is what the query layer and the filters match on — and that `uncategorizedId` is the field that tells the three apart.
files.why: The single render site that produces the duplicate-key warning. `recalculate.ts:127` already carries `uncategorizedId` onto every row, so no change to ReportOptions.ts is needed or wanted.

out_of_scope: ReportTableRow.tsx:98 `key={item.id}` is inert — it sits on the element the component returns, which is never an array child (RenderTableRow.tsx:36-44), so React ignores it and it cannot warn. It is worth deleting as a trap for the next reader, but it is not this bug and deleting it is a separate change.

The three synthetic rows each render a DOM element with `id=""` (ReportTableRow.tsx:110, `id={totalScrollRef ? 'total' : item.id}`), so the table carries three empty id attributes. That is an HTML validity wart, not a React key warning and not console noise. Fixing it means threading an identity helper into the DOM id, which changes ids QA selectors could rely on — its own ticket.

ReportTableList.tsx:55 keys the group rows by array index. Reordering the groups therefore makes React reuse the wrong rows. Index keys do not warn, and the rows hold no state, so it is latent rather than active — but it is a real reconciliation bug and a separate change.

The three synthetic rows' drilldown emits no category filter at all (showActivity.ts:73-79, `id && ...` is falsy on `''`), so clicking Uncategorized's amount shows unfiltered activity. That is existing behaviour this change deliberately preserves, and changing it is a product decision about what those rows should drill into, not a key fix.

CategorySelector.tsx:226 keys and matches on `category.id`. The report sidebar never passes it the synthetic group, so it is correct today. It becomes a duplicate-key site only if someone starts feeding it categoryLists() output — noted so that change is not made blind.

Confirm AC-2: the rows list shows the group header 'Uncategorized & Off budget' followed by three distinct rows 'Uncategorized', 'Transfers' and 'Off budget', each with its own amount. None is missing, none shows another's figure.

residual_risks: The change is confined to one key expression. If a future edit routes these three rows through a second id-keyed sibling list, the same warning returns there; the unit test only guards the site it covers.

The e2e guard is vacuous under a production React build, so CI coverage of AC-1 rests on Playwright running against `yarn start`. If that default ever changes, the guard silently stops testing anything and the jsdom unit test is all that is left.

validated_work_order.understanding:
A custom report appends three synthetic rows — Uncategorized (uncategorized_id 'other'), Transfers ('transfer') and Off budget ('off_budget') — in categoryLists() at packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/ReportOptions.ts:348-365, and parks them under the synthetic 'Uncategorized & Off budget' group (ReportOptions.ts:375-381). All three are declared `id: ''`, and the group they live in is the only one whose members are not keyed by a uuid.

The duplicate-key warning comes from exactly one render site. With Mode=Total, Viz=Data Table and the default Group by=Category, ReportTableList takes the grouped branch (ReportTableList.tsx:29-30, `data.groupedData`) and renders each group's members at ReportTableList.tsx:73-87 with `key={category.id}`. The uncategorized group therefore emits three sibling keys of `''` on every render, and React logs 'Encountered two children with the same key'. 'Show empty rows' is what makes it unconditional: without it, filterEmptyRows (filterEmptyRows.ts:16-24) drops the synthetic rows whose amounts are zero, so the three keys only collide when at least two of the three survive.

Two neighbouring `key={item.id}` uses look like candidates and are not. ReportTableRow.tsx:98 puts the key on the element the component returns, which is never an array child (RenderTableRow.tsx:36-44 renders it singly), so React ignores it. ReportTableHeader.tsx:87 and ReportTableList.tsx:55 key by index. CategorySelector.tsx:226 keys by id too, but the report sidebar feeds it `categories.grouped` straight from useCategories() (ReportSidebar.tsx:701-703), never categoryLists()' output, so the synthetic group never reaches it. Legend and chart rows key off name or dataKey (ReportLegend.tsx:45, calculateLegend.ts:70-73), which are already distinct for the three.

I could not execute anything to confirm the warning: this checkout has no node_modules, so no test or build runs. The claim is confirmed by reading the declarations and the single render site that consumes them, which is a closed set — three declared `id: ''` values, one `key={category.id}` over exactly those members.
